nodes.title: Consensus columns of a profile HMM

nodes.summary: Some path (alignment of `x` to the profile) has weight equal to the Viterbi value. Under nonnegative weights this attained value is the largest path weight (`pathProb_le_viterbi`); without that hypothesis attainment alone does not imply maximality.
nodes.title: The Viterbi value is attained

nodes.summary: The sum, over all alignments of `x` to the columns `[1, …, L]` (all paths through the model emitting `x`, each once), of the path weights.
nodes.title: Forward computes the total path weight

nodes.summary: The forward value of a sequence `x`: the total weight of all paths through the model that emit `x` (`forward_eq_sum`), by the recursion on one residue and one column.
nodes.title: Forward value of a sequence under a profile HMM

nodes.summary: HMMER's Plan 7 restrictions (Eddy 1998): no delete-to-insert and no insert-to-delete transitions, and no insert states at node `0` (the begin state) or node `L`.
nodes.title: HMMER Plan 7 restrictions

nodes.summary: Nonnegative transition and emission weights (the transitions to the end state may have any sign: the Viterbi bound does not need them).
nodes.title: Nonnegative weights of a profile HMM

nodes.summary: Every path weighs at most the Viterbi value.
nodes.title: Every path weighs at most the Viterbi value

nodes.summary: The weight of a path through the model, given as an alignment `A` of the sequence to the columns: the product of its transition and emission weights from the begin state to the end state.
nodes.title: Weight of a path through a profile HMM

nodes.summary: A profile HMM with `L` consensus columns over the alphabet `α`, with weights in `R`. `trans k s t` is the weight of a transition from the state of type `s` at node `k` (`0 ≤ k ≤ L`; node `0` is the begin state, read as type `M`) to a state of type `t`: to `M` or `D` at node `k + 1`, or to `I` at node `k`. `stop s` is the weight of the transition from the state of type `s` at node `L` to the end state.
nodes.title: Profile hidden Markov model

nodes.summary: The state types of a profile HMM node: match, insert, delete.
nodes.title: State types of a profile HMM node

nodes.summary: With positive pseudocounts, every residue gets a positive emission estimate, including residues absent from the column.
nodes.title: Pseudocount emission estimates are positive

nodes.summary: The emission estimate of a match state from the residues `col` that a multiple alignment places in its column (gaps omitted), with pseudocounts `pc` (Durbin et al., chapter 5; Laplace's rule is `pc = 1`): `(count a + pc a) / (|col| + ∑ b, pc b)`.
nodes.title: Pseudocount emission estimate of a match state

nodes.summary: With positive pseudocounts, the estimated emissions sum to one.
nodes.title: Pseudocount emission estimates sum to one

nodes.summary: A profile HMM with nonnegative weights is a nonnegative alignment automaton.
nodes.title: Nonnegative profile HMM gives a nonnegative alignment automaton

nodes.summary: The profile HMM as an alignment automaton reading alignments of a sequence to the columns `[1, …, L]`. The control state is the type of the previous state and the current node (the last column consumed); it starts at `(M, 0)`, the begin state. Reading `(some a, some j)` visits `M j`, `(some a, none)` visits the insert state of the current node, `(none, some j)` visits `D j`; the invalid column `(none, none)` has…
nodes.title: Profile HMM as an alignment automaton

nodes.summary: The Viterbi value of a sequence `x`: the value selected by the max recursion (`pathProb_le_viterbi`, `exists_pathProb_eq_viterbi`). Under nonnegative weights it is the largest weight of a path through the model emitting `x`.
nodes.title: Viterbi value of a sequence under a profile HMM

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
